findings.expected_vs_actual: Spec §7 says the sudo fallback only runs after EPERM, 'which never happens with runner-owned stubs'. On macOS, a runner-owned child that ignores SIGTERM and is then SIGKILLed at the grace makes the immediate follow-up group kill in the reap loop return EPERM (dying/zombie member), so retry logs 'retry: could not send SIGKILL to process group N (EPERM)' and runs a real 'sudo -n kill -s KILL -- -N' (observed via the CLI: 'retry: sudo could not send SIGKILL to process group N'). The outcome (timeouts, exit code, final error) is still correct and Linux CI is unaffected.
findings.fix: On a group made only of our own processes, retry should not call sudo (e.g. re-check groupExists / wait one poll before escalating, or only escalate when EPERM persists), so dev machines with cached sudo credentials do not run a root kill on a just-killed group.
